answer: Each agent’s voting weight can be tied to a unique, nontransferable credential issued only after a person completes an in-person challenge at an independent registrar. The credential is checked when an agent joins and cannot be reused across identities, so one operator must send people and pay the issuance fee for every extra vote. A karst region, a reef station, or a marble hall could host registrars; the geography may vary, but the bottleneck is scarce human verification, not an agent’s claimed name.
